A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SharpZO and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The CraFT comparison can be matched across its relocation, and the proofs are retained. V1's additional NeurIPS checklist does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLIP prompt-tuning experiments, distribution-shift evaluations, training-time measurements, and component and hyperparameter ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original accuracy, efficiency, robustness, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The sharpness-aware CMA-ES warm-up, CGE estimates, sparse RGE optimization, Z-pruning, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Equation (3) now explicitly evaluates the sharpness perturbation at theta_t, consistent with v1's Appendix D, Equation (9). This clarifies the existing method; the reported transition-setting change concerns experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 few-shot classification datasets and four ImageNet distribution-shift variants. The newly specified shot counts document existing coverage rather than establish a new task or population.

E2.justification: V2 adds CoOp to Table 2's distribution-shift comparison for both ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16. The other comparator memberships are retained. CraFT is not newly evaluated: its comparison moves from v1 Appendix C.3/Table 8 to v2 Section 5.4.3/Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported stage-transition selection from automatic early stopping to manually tuned values between 100 and 500 steps, retaining early stopping as an alternative. V2 Table 8 supplies dataset-specific transition steps. This is a reported protocol revision, without evidence establishing that the retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a brief qualitative check stating that automatic early stopping achieves results similar to manually tuned transition steps. Table 2 also extends the existing distribution-shift analysis with CoOp. The original sharpness, pruning, architecture, and hyperparameter analyses otherwise retain their evidence.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5.1 explicitly identifies Figure 1's bands as standard-deviation bands. V1 discusses lower variance and its checklist mentions shaded variance intervals without this specification. The plotted bands are unchanged, and neither version supplies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes official ZIP's ViT-B/16 Flowers102 accuracy from 92.30 to 70.40, reversing its reported ranking against SharpZO's unchanged 88.02. The ZIP average remains 70.57 despite the revised entries averaging approximately 68.58. Table 2 adds CoOp scores and distribution-shift averages; other retained numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorem 1, lemmas, convergence bounds, and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. Equation (3)'s mean notation and the replacement of E[z] with E[o] clarify existing expressions. The added CMA-ES background restates sampling mathematics already present in v1 Section 3.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same two-stage forward-only optimization contribution, sharpness-aware initialization and Z-pruning claims, and claimed accuracy and convergence benefits. The headline claim of up to 7% average improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 Section 5.1 newly interprets SharpZO as approaching first-order CoOp performance and connects this to practical deployment. Section 2.2 expands the explanation of covariance adaptation and population sampling as mechanisms for exploration. Appendix A's dimensionality and scalability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the default 16-shot setup, a 5-shot validation set and its source, hyperparameter-search candidate values and selection procedure, and dataset-specific transition steps. Most implementation settings and hardware information are retained. The direct code-repository footnote is replaced by a project-page link; the PDFs alone do not establish either resource's accessibility.

R1.justification: The new CMA-ES background adds Hansen and Ostermeier's 2001 paper and expands the comparison between evolutionary search and local ZO optimization. The remaining cited works and central novelty positioning are retained; reference renumbering does not represent additional literature changes.

P1.justification: V2 adds a CMA-ES background subsection, makes localized experimental-text revisions, moves Appendix C.3 into Section 5.4.3, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. It also corrects the CraFT discussion from time-to-accuracy to the memory measurement already shown in the table. Most scientific prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a CoOp row, average columns, and a caption restricting bold highlighting to BP-free methods. The hyperparameter table gains a transition-step row, and the CraFT table moves into the main text. Table highlighting and placement receive limited changes; all four figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility through explicit shot counts, validation-set construction, search grids, and transition settings, while the CoOp comparison supplies useful first-order context. These gains help readers reconstruct and assess the existing experiments. The improvement is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 3.3 still describes automatic switching, and Table 1's revised ZIP score leaves an internally inconsistent average.
